title: Ledger transfer service and its unit tests
name: Ledger transfer tests

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how these unit tests verify the transfer service's behavior? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
If `transfer` throws AccountFrozenError after locking both accounts, what does InMemoryLedger leave in `ledger.accounts` and `ledger.entries`?
choices: The debit is applied but no entries are recorded
Nothing changes: the snapshot and pending entries are discarded because the commit lines after `await fn(tx)` never run
Entries are recorded but balances are unchanged
Both accounts are marked frozen in the stored map

questions.prompt: Why does the test suite inject `() => FIXED_NOW` instead of letting TransferService call `new Date()`?
choices: new Date() is unavailable inside withTransaction
It makes the transfer faster in production
It lets the test assert the exact `postedAt` value deterministically, by identity
It forces both accounts to be locked in a consistent order

questions.prompt: The overdraft test calls `ledger.accounts.set("acc-b", ...)` inside the test. Why does this not affect other tests in the file?
choices: beforeEach builds a fresh InMemoryLedger and service for every test
Jest runs each `it` in a separate process
The Map is frozen after the first test
withTransaction restores the original accounts after each transfer
